business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture and Aseptic Tubing of Ambient Quick-Cook Tapioca Pearls

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; all corporate registration and name clearance centralized at the Registro Público de Panamá; no sub-state incorporation registries)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition) with marked United States commercial-law influence in banking and corporate matters; corporate and offshore regimes governed by Ley 32 de 1927 on Sociedades Anónimas, as amended by Ley 5 de 2019; unitary national jurisdiction without intra-country tax distinctions
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force since 31 October 2012, including investment and market-access protections
Panama–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty, in force since 1991
Panama–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)
Panama–Republic of Korea Double Taxation Agreement (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Panama's AML/CFT and UBO regime rests on: (i) Ley 32 de 1927 (General Corporate Law), as reformed by Ley 5 de 2019, imposing resident-agent custody of UBO records and regulating bearer-share custody; (ii) Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 on money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by Ley 70 de 2019 and Decreto Ley 2 de 4 de febrero de 2019; (iii) Ley 52 de 2016 creating the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSNF) as the AML supervisor of resident agents, corporate service providers, and trust companies; (iv) Decreto Ley 2 de 2019 creating the Registro de Personas Jurídicas, which requires every resident agent to file a Declaración de Beneficiario Final (UBO declaration) with beneficial-ownership information; and (v) applicable UAF/SSNF regulations on customer due diligence, risk classification, and suspicious-transaction reporting.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the certified passport of each incorporator, director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner (natural persons)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the holder's country of nationality (state passport office, national ID bureau, or embassy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for states party to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization at the nearest Panamanian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and constitutive documents of any corporate shareholder or body-corporate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or equivalent official corporate register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the Panamanian resident agent and attorney-in-fact to execute and register the incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the client's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (Carta de Referencia Bancaria) evidencing banking history and commercial probity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed and regulated commercial bank or financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized professional resume (hoja de vida) and source-of-funds declaration for each director, officer, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Natural person (with employer confirmation where possible), signature notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening under Ley 23 de 2015, as amended, and SSNF regulations; the resident agent must screen every incorporator, director, officer, authorized signatory, and UBO against: (a) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (b) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (c) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (d) Panama's domestic sanction designations and Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) advisories; and (e) commercial PEP databases. PEPs, including foreign and domestic PEPs and their close associates, trigger enhanced due diligence with senior-management approval; PEP status persists at least 12 months after termination of office. Negative media, sanctions matches, or complex nominee structures require enhanced CDD and, where indicia of ML/TF exist, a Suspicious Transaction Report (RTS) to the UAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Personas Jurídicas and online name consultation (Consulta de Nombres), accessible via the official portal www.registropublico.gob.pa; name-reservation applications and payments are processed electronically by the resident agent's accredited user account or through the Notaría Electrónica channel.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be formed in Spanish or in any foreign language using the Latin alphabet. Non-Latin-script names (e.g., Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) must be transliterated into Latin characters, and the transliterated form becomes the registered legal name. The name must contain an entity-type indicator such as 'S.A.', 'Corporación', 'Corp.', or 'Inc.'. The Registro Público refuses names that are identical or phonetically/visually confusingly similar to an existing registered entity, trademark-protected commercial designation, or reserved name. Punctuation, spacing, and abbreviations are strictly compared to prevent deceptive similarity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco — requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
Seguros / Reaseguros — requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros
Bolsa / Valores / Fondo / Fondos de Inversión — requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores
Fideicomiso / Trust / Fiduciaria — restricted financial-services tokens requiring SSNF or financial-supervisor approval
Caja de Ahorro / Financiera / Crédito — banking-adjacent tokens requiring prior financial-supervisory authorization
Nacional / Presidencia / Gobierno / Estado / Ministerio / Policía / Ejército — restricted due to implied official connection with the Republic of Panama
Canal de Panamá / Zona Libre de Colón / Ciudad Libre de Colón — restricted names requiring authorization from the Panama Canal Authority or the Colon Free Zone administration
Lotería / Casino / Juego — restricted tokens requiring prior gaming-control authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the resident agent files a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) before the Dirección General Registral within five (5) business days of notification, attaching the official name-search certificate and a legal memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from the conflicting registered name. Alternatively, the applicant may file a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) with the Director General of the Registro Público within the same five-business-day window. The Registro Público must decide within thirty (30) business days. In parallel, counsel should reserve one or two alternative names to avoid delaying incorporation. Where rejection arises from a third-party's reserved or registered name, a notarized letter of consent from that third party may be submitted with a fresh name-clearance application. Short-term extensions of the 30-day reservation are available upon re-application and payment of the applicable tariff before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with limitations: every Panama S.A. must maintain a licensed resident agent and a registered office, which statutorily may be the resident agent's own office address; a purely virtual address arrangement is therefore legally acceptable for the registered office. However, for ISIC 1030 manufacturing activity (canned boba/tapioca pearls), the entity must document actual operational substance if it derives Panamanian territorial-source income, files an aviso de operación, or applies for public-health (Ministerio de Salud) and food-import/export permits. Pure foreign-source income falls outside Panama's territorial tax net, but a 'brass-plate' profile with no plausible source-of-funds narrative will trigger enhanced due diligence by financial institutions and the SSNF rather than outright prohibition.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk for this industry: approximately 5–10% cumulative probability in the first three registration years. Registro Público and SSNF conduct mostly paper-based or targeted inspections of resident agents' AML files rather than unannounced on-site visits to shareholders' or production premises. Unannounced inspections become materially more likely if a suspicious-transaction report, negative media report, or FATF-driven inspection wave implicates the resident agent or the client.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and Certificate of Name Availability (Certificado de Disponibilidad de Nombre)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff (arancel) for name-clearance certificates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Execution of the public deed of incorporation (Escritura Pública) before a Panamanian Notary Public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: State notarial tariff for corporate deeds, protocol, and seal charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the incorporation deed with the Registro Público de Panamá (inscripción de título constitutivo)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal review, stamp duties, and administrative fees for the incorporation file (derechos de revisión and timbres)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market professional fee for UBO piercing, CDD, and sanctions/PEP screening under Ley 23 de 2015 and SSNF/GAFILAT practice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent and registered office service, first-year fee (agente residente y sede registrada, primer año)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm or corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market fee for professional resident-agency services, including statutory presence, mail handling, and annual franchise-tax administration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of the identity/corporate document bundle (five documents)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas), as amended; relevant provisions of the Código de Comercio (arts. 149–158); Ley 5 de 1997 (corporations subject to Public Registry supervision); Ley 62 de 2016 (beneficial ownership disclosure)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas, Departamento de Registro de Sociedades
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Articles of Incorporation / Pacto Social y Estatutos), followed by inscription at the Public Registry and issuance of the Certificado de Registro
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital; an authorized capital of USD 10,000 divided into registered shares is standard. No escrow account or bank deposit is required at incorporation; subscription payment may be deferred and recorded in the corporate ledger.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION No. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY] S.A., unanimously adopted on [DATE] at the registered office in Panama. The Board resolves: (1) to ratify the share subscriptions recorded in the Share Register; (2) to adopt [ADDRESS], City of Panama, as the registered office; (3) to appoint [DIRECTOR 1] as President, [DIRECTOR 2] as Secretary, and [DIRECTOR 3] as Treasurer for the statutory term; (4) to authorize the Officers, acting jointly, to execute banking resolutions, commercial contracts, and corporate filings; (5) to open a corporate bank account; and (6) to apply for the sanitary, environmental, municipal, and fire-safety licenses required for the tapioca pearls processing plant. Approved by all Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Mercantile Name Section / online portal www.registropublico.gob.pa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for two proposed corporate names. The Registry checks the mercantile index for identical or confusingly similar names. Approved names are reserved for 30 calendar days. Ensure the corporate objects clause expressly covers processing and aseptic packing of tapioca pearls.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre)
Copy of identity document or passport of each subscriber
Notarized power of attorney, if submitted by a legal representative or law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a fresh application with alternative names. A conflicting registered name may be overcome by filing the written consent of the prior registrant or a court-ordered cancellation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution and Legalization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (any active Panamanian notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Pacto Social y Estatutos in Spanish, including corporate name, registered office, general and specific corporate purpose covering the manufacture of canned boba tapioca pearls, share capital, and initial board. Execute the Escritura Pública before a Panamanian notary with at least three natural subscribers or two corporate subscribers. Obtain the certified first copy (testimonio) for Public Registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos)
Passport or ID of each subscriber and director
Certificate of existence and notarized power of attorney for corporate subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to any clause, amend the bylaws by addendum or execute a rectification deed prior to registration; foreign-language documents must be accompanied by certified Spanish translations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public Registry Inscription of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas (Mercantile Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarial testimonio of the Escritura de Constitución together with the Registry's legal fee form (orden de pago). Pay the graduated inscription fee based on authorized capital, and obtain the stamped inscription entry and the Certificado de Registro recognizing the legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial first copy (testimonio) of the Escritura de Constitución
Completed Registry legal fee order form and payment receipt
Report of name reservation and Registry-issued clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a 'nota de defecto', cure the noted deficiency within the statutory term (generally 10 business days) or file a reconsideration appeal; repeated rejection may be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Books Legalization and Tax Registration (RUC and Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Registro Público for corporate book inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation as a taxpayer to obtain the RUC, file the sworn 'Aviso de Operación' for the food manufacturing activity, and inscribe the corporate Minute Book, Share Register, and Ledger at the Public Registry within one month of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificado de Registro)
DGI Form 01 (taxpayer registration) and Form 05 (Aviso de Operación)
Copy of the legal representative's identity and appointment
Lease or ownership verification of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI withholds registration or issues an inconsistency, file an amendment to the Aviso de Operación and present supporting documents; a suspended RUC may be reactivated within 10 days upon payment of nominal penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación Municipal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of the registered seat, e.g., Municipio de Panamá – Tesorería Municipal and Fiscalización
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the municipal Aviso de Operación declaring the industrial/commercial activity, pay the proportional municipal patent tax based on estimated gross revenue, and obtain the municipal operating permit valid for the corresponding fiscal year.
required_dossiers: DGI RUC certificate and Aviso de Operación
Certificate of Incorporation from the Public Registry
Lease agreement or proof of ownership of the premises
Fire brigade inspection certificate (Visto Bueno de Bomberos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal inspection finds deficiencies, remediate building and safety conditions and request re-inspection; patent tax base disputes may be contested before the municipal tax authorities or administrative courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security Employer Registration (Caja de Seguro Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) – Dirección General de Afiliación y Registro Patronal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation as an employer with the CSS by filing the employer inscription application, attaching corporate documents and the legal representative's IDs. Obtain the employer registry number to enable payroll contributions once staff are hired.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate from DGI
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Legal representative appointment resolution and ID/passport
CSS employer registration form (Form 690)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSS application is queried, present the corrected official appointment resolution, update the Public Registry extract, and re-submit the employer file; any delay in registration may be cured by backdated contribution payments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección General de Salud, Departamento de Regulación y Fiscalización de Alimentos y Bebidas
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Sanitaria de Funcionamiento and Registro Sanitario de Alimentos (Sanitary Operating License and Food Product Sanitary Registration)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Costos Ambientales / Departamento de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I (Ficha Ambiental / Environmental Notice) for small-scale aseptic canning lines; Categoría II (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental, EsIA) where installed production capacity exceeds 500 kg/day, where significant trade-effluent discharge is expected, or where steam boilers exceed threshold capacities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Decreto Ejecutivo 189 de 1998 (continental waters protection): BOD5 ≤ 350 mg/L, COD ≤ 700 mg/L, TSS ≤ 300 mg/L, pH 6–9; air emissions per Decreto Ejecutivo 163 de 1999 (PM10 ≤ 150 µg/Nm³, VOC and combustion-gas thresholds for boilers); solid waste management per Ley 6 de 2018 with mandatory manifest of food-processing by-products.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Visto Bueno del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá) prior to municipal licensing; structural load inspection and occupancy clearance issued by the municipality for industrial premises; occupational health and safety inspection by MITRADEL under the Reglamento de Seguridad e Higiene Industrial covering steam-boiler certification, machinery guarding, and worker exposure controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; electronic portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (Sede Electrónica)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.), the foreign shareholders must: (1) execute a public deed of incorporation before a Panamanian notary and file it with the Public Registry through a licensed registered agent; (2) appoint a resident legal officer and maintain a registered office in Panama; (3) obtain a municipal business license (aviso de operación) from the local municipality; (4) register with the DGI within 30 days of commencing operations using the Sede Electrónica portal, submitting the deeds, business license, appointment documents, and proof of legal representation; (5) receive the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) certificate, which serves as the corporate TIN and VAT (ITBMS) identification; and (6) apply for DGI digital signature and electronic-invoice authorization credentials.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box entity classification election or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Panamanian law; an S.A. is per se a corporation taxed at entity level on Panama-source income. Available elections include notional tax assimilation to a small taxpayer / simplified ITBMS fixed-fee regime where annual gross turnover does not exceed B/.100,000, election to be governed by the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) tax stability regime, and election to operate under the Panama Pacifico Special Economic Area regime if qualifying; no independent fiscal-transparency election is recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panama's VAT/GST equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No annual threshold exemption for registration: any person habitually transferring taxable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must register for ITBMS with the DGI. A simplified small-taxpayer regime is available to those with annual gross turnover not exceeding B/.100,000, reducing compliance obligations but not eliminating the RUC/ITBMS registration requirement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for taxpayers selected by DGI as electronic invoicing agents, operating through the Sede Electrónica portal or certified third-party software connected via DGI-approved API. Invoices must carry a DGI-granted authorization code and be transmitted in near-real-time at issue; acceptance or rejection is communicated digitally for fiscal clearance. Digital stamping/QR validation is required on invoices supporting input tax credits and export zero-rating claims. Phased integration covers large taxpayers first, with mandatory digital filing of all B2B invoices completed under DGI's schedule.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero rate (0% ITBMS) applies to the physical export of goods from Panama where the exporter is registered for ITBMS, the goods are transported across the border under a valid customs declaration, and title or physical control passes to a foreign purchaser. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated only where the service is effectively used or consumed outside Panama and the recipient is not a Panamanian resident; documentary proof of external consumption must be retained. The exporter must have fully complied with RUC and electronic-invoicing obligations at the time of shipment and must apply the zero rate only upon exercising reasonable due diligence as to the export nature of the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera, DUA) validated by the National Customs Authority
Bill of Lading (original ocean or air waybill evidencing cross-border shipment)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT payment receipt showing export proceeds received from abroad
Commercial invoice issued under the electronic-invoicing regime with DGI authorization code
Packing list and certificate of origin (if required or claimed)
Export contract or purchase order of the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and the National Customs Authority jointly audit export zero-rating claims with heightened scrutiny of canned-tapioca and other processed-food exporters routed through free zones. If an exporter is found to have simulated exports, submitted false customs declarations, or failed to telegraphically repatriate export proceeds within the statutory window, the zero rate is retroactively denied and the standard 7% ITBMS is clawed back with moratory interest and surcharge. Administrative penalties scale to 50%-100% of the evaded tax; severe or repeated fraud exposes the S.A. to criminal liability for tax evasion under Panama's Tax Criminal Law, including potential imprisonment of the legal representative, suspension of the RUC, cancellation of the export registration, and forfeiture of goods. Exporters are required to retain the full documentation bundle for at least six years after export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama maintains no central bank and does not issue domestic paper currency; monetary and banking supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), while the Banco Nacional de Panamá performs the role of fiscal agent and clearing agent for the Republic. Official tender comprises the Panamanian Balboa (PAB), which circulates solely as a fixed 1:1 subdivision of the United States dollar (USD), with USD itself legal tender under Article 158 of the Political Constitution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic is fully dollarized, meaning there is no independent exchange-rate policy and therefore no administrative block on currency conversion. Capital and current account convertibility are unrestricted: foreign investors may open USD and multi-currency accounts, purchase and sell any foreign currency at SBP-licensed bank market rates, and remit dividends, capital, interest, and management fees without exchange-control approval. Practical frictions are documentary and fiscal rather than regulatory: remittances abroad to non-residents for deductible payments are subject to a 10% remittance tax under Articles 762-A and 763 of the Tax Code, dividends attributable to Panamanian-source profits are subject to a 5% withholding tax, and banks apply standard source-of-funds due diligence on outbound wires. For a tapioca-pearl exporter collecting proceeds in USD, conversion and repatriation are functionally frictionless.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama does not impose mandatory export-proceeds surrender, no minimum percentage conversion obligation, and no statutory term for repatriation of export receipts. An exporting S.A. may retain USD and any freely convertible currency in domestic or offshore accounts indefinitely, may apply those proceeds directly to settle foreign suppliers for cassava starch, sugar, packaging, and aseptic-tubing equipment, and may convert surplus at negotiated bank rates. Only standard transaction-level AML verification and customs-document reconciliation apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium as a primary banking rail; Medium as an ancillary settlement channel. Under Decreto Ley 9 de 1998 and SBP regulation, only licensed banks may intermediately receive deposits or provide full payment services in Panama; unlicensed offshore EMIs (UK, EU, or Singapore e-money firms) cannot lawfully operate as the treasury core for a Panamanian operating S.A., although they may clear low-value payments if funds transit a licensed correspondent bank. Panama-based digital-fintech products remain captive to sponsoring SBP-regulated banks. Recommendation: use bank-fintech hybrids for disbursement convenience only, never as the sole receiving account for export proceeds or as the LC issuing vehicle; always retain a Tier-1 local bank as principal clearing and credit anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Agreement 4-2019 impose full customer due diligence on all directors, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners holding 10% or more. Fully remote onboarding without any interaction is unavailable; Tier-1 banks generally permit live video-identity verification combined with notarized and apostilled corporate kit, but in practice a physical or notarized interview of at least one director is expected for the first operational account. Because a tapioca-pearl manufacturer is a low ML-risk commercial client, banks will commonly accept remote interview plus a supervisory bank reference; however, establishing a capital escrow and later a trade-limit increase may require a physical visit to the Panama City branch and presentation of original Escritura Pública documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and UBOs combined with Panama's historic offshore-perception profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies (notarized and apostilled); Escritura Pública of the S.A. and registered amendments (Registro Público); certificate of good standing and paz y salvo; signed ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration per Law 23 of 2015; foreign tax-residence certificate; source-of-wealth statement; six-to-twelve months bank reference letters from the shareholder's existing bank; MINSA food-operation permit; commercial license demonstrating active manufacturing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Historical bearer-share or Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) ownership opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written confirmation that no bearer shares are outstanding and that all shares were migrated to nominative format under Law 254 of 2015; complete share register; foundation charter and current council minutes if a PIF is involved; economic-beneficiary declaration filed through the SBP/Known-Your-Customer channel; board resolution identifying banking signatories; no-asset exemption certificate if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-pattern mismatches between declared tapioca starch/pearl shipments and wire/LC values.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed export sales contracts; commercial invoices and pro-forma invoices; ocean/airway bills of lading; packing lists; pre-shipment inspection certificates; certificates of origin; HACCP/ISO 22000 and FDA/GRAS or EU food-safety attestations; customs export declarations from SIGA/e-Tunes; laboratory batch-test records for aseptic-tubed quick-cook pearls; supplier purchase contracts for cassava starch, sugar, and packaging matched against booked costs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque source of inbound capital injection (equity vs shareholder loan ambiguity).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-contribution board minutes (acta de aporte); updated share premium and paid-in-capital schedule; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the contributing parent; bank reference confirming source of wealth; copy of the SWIFT MT103 with purpose field referencing aporte de capital; shareholder tax declaration of residency; escrow release instruction letter signed by all directors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity is wired by the shareholder's overseas bank via SWIFT MT103 to the Panamanian S.A.'s designated account (capital escrow account at Banco Nacional de Panamá or operational account at Banco General). Beneficiary line must match the S.A.'s registered legal name and CIF/RUC identifier; purpose description should read CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / APORTES DE CAPITAL to distinguish equity from intercompany debt. No central-bank authorization or FX declaration is required because Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction; the receiving bank will hold funds pending release on corporate-resoluce verification, source-of-funds declaration, and UBO confirmation. Capital inflows exceeding USD 10,000 per transaction are automatically reportable under SBP cash-reporting thresholds; for injections above USD 1,000,000, a board resolution and notarized shareholder decisions should be pre-delivered to the relationship manager to avoid funds-on-hold delays.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements run over SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier prepayments and over irrevocable sight Commercial Letters of Credit (issued by the Panamanian bank via Swift MT700 to beneficiary banks in Vietnam, Thailand, China, or Brazil) for large cassava-starch, sugar, packaging, and aseptic-tubing equipment purchases. Panama's domestic clearing infrastructure (Cámara de Compensación and Banco Nacional as clearing agent) settles USD book-entry transfers same day, but cross-border trade requires the SWIFT correspondent network. LC documentary review must align commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, inspection certificate, and insurance certificate; field 72 of the MT103 should name the underlying goods as FOOD-ISIC 1030 TAPIOCA PEARL RAW MATERIALS to facilitate counterparty sanctions and AML screening on the beneficiary bank's side. Payment terms of 30- to 60-day LC at sight are recommended for the first 12 months before converting suppliers to clean TT terms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) to neutralize RMB-denominated starch and packaging cost exposure
USD/BRL Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for Brazilian cassava-starch procurement
USD/VND Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) quoted by regional treasury desks for Southeast Asian supplier costs
Cross-currency swaps (USD vs CNY or USD vs BRL) with an SBP-licensed bank to convert large capex funding tranches
OTC European-style FX options (call/put) for contingent aseptic-tubing equipment purchases
ISDA-governed forward currency purchases of USD against freely convertible majors where a physical settlement corridor exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate franchise tax (Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Dirección General de Ingresos e-Pago portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through March 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late surcharge of 10% up to a maximum of 50% plus statutory interest; persistent non-payment beyond 90 days permits administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos – Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31; immediate update required within 30 calendar days of any shareholding or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 10,000 or 2% of net assets, suspension of taxpayer registration services, and restriction on conducting corporate acts before the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración Jurada Anual de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – taxpayer portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 15 for calendar-year taxpayers; within three months after fiscal year-end, or on the general extension date published by DGI, for non-calendar fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 10% to 100% of the tax due, monthly interest at the legal rate, enforced collection by distraint and seizure, and criminal sanction for fraudulent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statement submission (Estados Financieros with the renta declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the annual income tax return no later than March 15; for non-essential offshore-only companies, an affidavit of no Panamanian-source income may be accepted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic presumption of taxable income by DGI, penalties up to 200% of assessed tax, and placement of the corporate taxpayer in a non-compliant status restricting certificates and municipal licenses.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No blanket statutory audit for all private Sociedades Anónimas. Independent audit by a certified public accountant is mandatory for companies in regulated financial sectors, public-interest entities, and any company whose gross revenue exceeds USD 300,000 or total assets exceeds USD 500,000 when DGI requires audited financial statements; additionally, shareholder agreements, financing covenants, or board resolutions may impose audit requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by IASB maintained by the Panamanian Accounting Standards Board; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para Pymes) is expressly permitted for non-public manufacturing companies within SME thresholds; all accounting records must comply with the Panama Commercial Code and Tax Code.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 238 of 2019, each Sociedad Anónima must file a sworn annual declaration of beneficial owners with DGI's RBF portal, identifying all natural persons who ultimately own or control more than 10% of shares, voting rights, or effective economic ownership. The declaration must be reconfirmed each year by March 31; any transfer of shareholding or change in control must be reported within 30 calendar days. The resident agent is statutory custodian of the supporting UBO file at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Brazilian Beneficial Owner Register per Law 70/2019

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Impuesto sobre la Renta, ISR) on Panama-source taxable income; territorial system excludes foreign-source income from assessment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial 0% rate on foreign-source export margins; 100% ISR exemption for up to 15 years if the factory is located in the Panama Pacifico Special Economic Area; accelerated write-offs and the 4% minimum 'complementary dividend' mechanism eliminate the risk of exit tax on retained profits; investments in agro-industrial cassava supply chains may access preferential deductions under Law 28 of 1995.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 348 (Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta) submitted via the DGI e-filing portal 'SITTI' (Sistema de Transacciones Tributarias Interactivas) at SITTI.DGI.GOB.PA; the legacy T@PAN portal remains available for read-only retrieval.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year ending 31 December unless the DGI authorizes a different fiscal year). Monthly 'anticipos' (advance payments) are required for corporations whose prior-year tax exceeded USD 5,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before 15 March for calendar-year taxpayers (the last business day if 15 March falls on a weekend or a national holiday); equivalent to three months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 (Identificación del Contribuyente / RUC y DV)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (13-character RUC) and verification digit; company legal name; ISIC economic activity code (1030 for manufacture of preserved process foods).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Panama S.A.'s RUC originally obtained upon incorporation at the DGI; the 4% advance dividend payment and the $300 franchise fee must be current before the SITTI return is accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales revenue from activities performed in Panama, including sales of canned boba tapioca pearls to domestic distributors and to shipping companies in Panama ports.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all invoices issued by the Panamanian S.A. for deliveries ex-works Panama; do not net out freight, insurance, or commissions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue derived from economic activities performed entirely outside Panama. For a manufacturing exporter this box normally remains zero unless the taxpayer operates a foreign sales branch.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim treaty benefits or territorial exemptions the taxpayer must attach contracts, bills of lading and cargo manifests proving the economic activity occurred abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: tapioca starch, sweeteners, food-grade sodium benzoate, aseptic pouches, cans, lids, factory salaries, power, water, sterilization costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-residents will be disallowed unless the Panamanian payer has applied the 12.5% gross WHT on royalties/interest/technical fees and the payee submitted its DGI tax domicile form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income after allowable deductions and the five-year loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the territorial regime, compute exclusively from Panamanian-source items; do not mix global income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complementary dividend tax assessed at 10% over the excess, if any, between 40% of the taxable net income and the dividends actually distributed in the fiscal year; this creates a minimum 4% annual charge on undistributed profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are subject to the same computational rule; the 10% withholding on paid dividends is a final tax not creditable against the shareholder's home-country corporate tax unless a treaty provides otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 19 (Total Impuesto a Pagar y Anticipos)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax due before deducting provisional 'anticipos' already paid on a monthly basis and any tax withheld by the DGI on banking interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The net payable is paid in USD (Balboa equivalent) through the SITTI portal using a Panamanian bank account or cash at Banco Nacional de Panamá.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual transfer pricing disclosure form: identification of related parties, amounts of controlled transactions, method applied (TNMM, Resale Price, Cost Plus, CUP, Profit Split) and tested-party position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This annex must be signed by a licensed Panamanian public accountant. Absent a Local File for transactions exceeding USD 500,000, the DGI may adjust the price and apply a 50% penalty on the deficiency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax plus monthly recargos of 1% on the unpaid balance; disconnection of the RUC for import/export operations; publication on the DGI public debtor list and travel-ban certificates issued through the Fiscal Code enforcement procedure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10.0% final withholding tax on dividends distributed out of Panama-taxable retained earnings; 20.0% final withholding tax on dividends paid from exempt or foreign-source income where the segregated accounting election was not perfected. A minimum 4% complementary dividend tax applies annually on undistributed taxable net income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty-reduced dividend rates, the beneficial-owner shareholder must (1) obtain a fiscal residence certificate (TRC) from its country of residence, (2) execute DGI Form 723 'Solicitud de Aplicación de Tratado para Evitar la Doble Imposición' through a duly registered 'apoderado' in Panama, (3) attach audited proof of beneficial ownership (or chain-of-ownership certificate for listed entities), and (4) receive the DGI resolution granting the reduced rate before the dividend payment is booked; the withholding agent must keep minutes of the shareholder resolution and the TRC for at least five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT: 12.5% gross basis on interest and IP royalties remitted to non-residents (including mingling payments for technical assistance, brand royalties for the boba brand, and financing from a Caribbean treasury company). Under Panama's DTA network, interest rates may fall to 5%–10% and royalties to 5%–10% on gross, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner; payments to listed tax haven jurisdictions remain subject to the surcharge regime under Article 725 of the Fiscal Code.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 500,000 per fiscal year in aggregate related-party cross-border transactions (Panama is fully dollarized; the threshold is stated in USD). Multinational groups with consolidated revenue equal to or above USD 800 million (approx. EUR 750 million) must also prepare a Country-by-Country Report and the local Master File, to be filed via the SITTI portal within 12 months from fiscal year-end.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not enact Economic Substance Regulations modeled on the UAE Crown Dependency rules. Nevertheless, the Fiscal Code territorial test (Article 693) plus the DGI anti-avoidance doctrine and the 2015 'Materialidad Económica' rulings require: (1) management staff and commercial decisions physically sit in Panama; (2) the production plant has own industrial equipment, food-safety licenses (DIGESA/ARSENA Panama), and independent personnel; and (3) the S.A. can evidence operating substance if invoicing the canned boba product on a principal basis rather than as a commisionaire. Pure pass-through invoicing will be recharacterized under the 'substance over form' jurisprudence and the taxpayer may lose both treaty relief and the territorial advantage on the export margin.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Aggressive Misreporting of Panama-Source Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording a fake foreign-source distribution to sweep the canned-boba export margin out of the Panamanian tax net; issuing 'nota de remesa' credit notes to mask intercompany sales; two sets of accounts for aseptic tubing deliveries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal Code Article 748-A: administrative fine of 50% to 300% of the evaded tax; monthly recargos; criminal penalty under Código Penal Article 287: 3 to 10 years' imprisonment where the concealed amount exceeds USD 100,000, plus conviction for 'fraud against public administration' under Article 288 with disqualification from contracting with the State for five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panama's civil courts have regularly pierced the corporate veil for fraud (Sociedades Anónimas Law 32 of 1927, Article 58); directors who signed false returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency; the DGI can obtain an embargo (attachment) over personal assets and a salida del país (exit ban) via the 'medidas de apremio' under the Fiscal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominee resident agent, a mailbox in the City of Knowledge, and an offshore shareholder foundation (PIF) with no board minutes, no contract files, and no payroll in Panama for the so-called 'principal' manufacturing operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the entire canned-boba supply chain; denial of the territorial exemption; 100% surcharge on deductions paid to tax havens (Fiscal Code Article 725); revocation of the 'Aviso de Operación' (business notice) and the DIGESA food-plant license; the company may additionally be blacklisted as 'sociedad sin actividad reportada' under the Registro Público's final beneficiary system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominal directors of the Panamanian S.A. cannot hide behind the corporate form once the DGI proves the company acted as a fictitious conduit (Jurisprudencia: Corte Suprema adopts the 'lifting of the veil' doctrine); directors may be summoned by the criminal AML court, their residence visas revoked, and they incur personal civil restitution to trade-creditor victims up to the full value of the containers of tapioca pearls wrongfully invoiced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Missing Transfer Pricing Documentation / Sham Intercompany Margin
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing the Curaçao or Hong Kong buying agent at a 45% resale margin where the tested Panamanian manufacturer retains only a 3% residual; failure to prepare the Local File although related-party flows exceed USD 500,000; use of the 'Cost Plus' method without benchmarked comparables for aseptic beverage additives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI transfer pricing audit adjustment with automatic 50% penalty on the adjustment (Article 762-J); interest and recargos; exclusion from the e-invoicing system; and for habitual offenders, publication on the 'DGI lista negra' that blocks governmental export certification (SILECE).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the intercompany price are attributable under the 'managing partner' doctrine; the DGI recourse extends to personal bank accounts where the profits were routed through shareholder loans; a criminally culpable director faces 4 to 10 years under the AML statute if the artificial margin is used to launder proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / UBO Transparency Breach (Trade-Based Money Laundering)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the canned-boba export trade to conceal proceeds: over-invoicing tapioca pearl shipments to an affiliated food importer, receiving payment from shell bank accounts in jurisdictions on the FATF grey list, or failing to declare the ultimate beneficial owner in the Registro Público's 'SIBO' platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 (as amended by Law 70 of 2019): fines per infraction from USD 10,000 up to USD 1 million for the S.A.; criminal money-laundering for amounts exceeding USD 10,000 with commercial cover-up carries 5 to 12 years' imprisonment (Código Penal Article 254); the UAF may freeze the company's cargo and bank balances without prior court order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors designated as 'representante legal' are personally criminally liable if they knowingly sign invoices for fictitious food-grade boba cargo; they may be barred from leaving Panama (travel ban issued by the Fiscal Court), placed on the INTERPOL red list, and disgorged of any bonuses received; the ultimate foreign beneficial owner loses the shield of the PIF and becomes subject to extradition risk.
